From the log I read this run as a pass on the part that matters, with three things that fell short. Tell me which one you counted as the failure, or if it was something else.

**What worked**
- The `flock` ran alone, before any fetch. The session made no fetch, no `jj st`, and no messages read.
- It saw exit code 1, stopped, and said another session holds the lock. My holder was never disturbed.

**What fell short**
- **It read `.vc-config.md` and `TODO.md` before taking the lock.** These are reads only and change nothing, but they are not "before anything else".
- **Its "still running" check was useless.** It ran `pgrep`, which only sees its own sandbox, so it learned nothing and dumped a screen of noise. It only found out from the exit notice, which happened to arrive before it moved on. My wording said "confirms it is still running" without saying how.
- **It offered a way around the lock.** Its last line was "If no other session is actually running in this workspace, tell me and say how you want to proceed." The suggested prompt you saw, "no other session is running, continue the acquaint", is Claude Code's autocomplete built from that sentence. The session did not act on it, but one keypress would have overridden the lock.

**Proposed fix**
Make the check synchronous, and close the escape hatch:

> Lock: at acquaint, before anything else, a session runs `flock -xn .agent-running true` at the workspace root, alone. If it fails, another session holds the lock: the session reports that, does nothing further, and offers no way around it, since clearing a stale lock is the user's to do. If it succeeds, the session starts `flock -xn .agent-running sleep infinity` as a background command, leaves it running, and reports that it started. A session that already holds one does neither. …

The probe returns its answer in the foreground, so there is no waiting on a notice and no `pgrep`. The catch is a small gap between the probe and the holder in which two sessions starting in the same second could both pass; the loser's holder would then exit, and the line would still need to say that an exit means stop.

I have not changed `custom.md`. Say whether to put this in.

One aside: `../lock-experiment.txt` contains that session's sandbox proxy tokens in the `pgrep` output. They are local to that session, but the file is best deleted and not shared.

content.text:
That whole block is the output of one command, not a list of things the session did. Nothing in it touched your files.

**What happened**
- The session ran `pgrep -af 'flock -xn .agent-running'` to see if its lock holder was alive. `pgrep -a` prints the full command line of every process that matches.
- It matched itself. Every command Claude runs is wrapped in a sandbox program called `bwrap` (bubblewrap), and the command being run is passed to `bwrap` as an argument. So the text `flock -xn .agent-running` appeared inside the wrapper's own command line, and `pgrep` printed that command line: lines 23 to 102 are process 1, the wrapper, and lines 103 to 109 are process 2, the shell inside it.
- It never saw the real holder. That is the "liveness check failed" the session reported.

**What the flags mean**
They are the sandbox's setup, the same for every command either of us runs:

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--ro-bind A B` | Read-only bind mount, as you guessed: host path A is visible inside the sandbox at B and cannot be written. It starts with `--ro-bind / /`, the whole filesystem read-only. |
| `--bind A B` | The same, writable. These are the few places a command may write: the workspace, `/tmp`, `~/.cargo`, `~/.config/jj`. |
| `--tmpfs P` | An empty in-memory directory placed over P, hiding the real one. `~/.ssh` is hidden this way, with only the commit-signing key and `known_hosts` bound back in. |
| `--unshare-pid` | The command gets its own process numbering and sees only its own processes. This is why `pgrep` found just processes 1 and 2. |
| `--unshare-net` | No direct network; traffic goes through the proxy named in the `--setenv` lines. |
| `--die-with-parent` | The sandbox is killed when Claude Code exits, which is why the lock holder should die with its session. |

The long run of `--ro-bind` lines after the writable ones re-protects specific files inside the workspace, such as `.claude/settings.json`, `.git/config` and `.git/hooks`, so a command cannot change its own permissions.

The probe wording I proposed removes this: with `flock -xn .agent-running true` answering in the foreground, the session has no reason to go looking for a process.

The plain version: the session asked "is my lock process running?", the question only found itself, and the screenful is the sandbox's settings being printed back.

The probe wording is in `custom.md`, wrapped under 100 columns (the longest line is 97). I also added three lines to the `TODO.md` entry saying why the probe and the fixed sentence exist, citing what the two earlier runs did.

Ready for the third run. Start a second Claude here and say "acquaint". The pass is:

- One command before anything but the `custom.md` read: `flock -xn .agent-running true`.
- One sentence in reply: "Another session holds `.agent-running`, stopping."
- Nothing after it: no background holder, no `pgrep`, no fetch, no offer to continue.

It will probably still read `.vc-config.md` and `TODO.md` in the same batch as `custom.md`, since it cannot know the lock rule until it has read the file that states it. Those are reads and change nothing; I would not count them against the run.

Tell me when it has run and I will read its transcript.

message.content: Should I run acquaint again or /exit then acquaint, both are worth doing, I think

content.text:
Both, in this order, since exiting ends the first option:

1. **"acquaint" again in the session that is still open.** It re-reads `custom.md`, so it gets the new wording. This tests a reacquaint in a session that holds no lock: it should run the probe, fail, and give the one sentence. It is the weaker test, because that session already knows it was refused and may answer from memory instead of running the probe. The transcript will show which.
2. **`/exit`, then a fresh session and "acquaint".** This is the real test: a session with no history meeting the new line cold.

There is a third case worth running afterwards, and it is mine to do: a "reacquaint" in this session, which holds the lock. It tests "a session that already holds one does neither". If I ran the probe here it would be refused by my own holder and I would wrongly announce another session, so the pass is that I skip both commands and carry on. Say "reacquaint" when you want that.

Tell me after each run and I will read its transcript.

Its two tool calls on the second "acquaint":

| Time (UTC) | Call |

| 20:26:27 | `flock -xn .agent-running sleep infinity`, in the background |
| 20:26:30 | Read that command's output file |

Two findings from it:

- **A reacquaint can skip the `custom.md` read.** [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint) step 1 says to read it, and this session did not, presumably because it had the file in context from 16 minutes earlier. That is a miss against the rule as written, and it means an edit to `custom.md` does not reach a session that is already open unless something forces the read.
- **The lock still held.** Even on stale instructions it was refused and did nothing else.

The new wording is still untested. The fresh run is the one that counts: `/exit` that session, start a new one, and say "acquaint".

| Time (UTC) | Call |
|---|---|
| 20:29:43 | Read `custom.md`, `.vc-config.md`, `TODO.md` |

- The probe came first, alone, before any fetch.
- No background holder was started.

A small tightening would close it. In the `custom.md` line, change

> … and does nothing further.

to

> … and runs no further command, not even to find the holder.

Your call whether that is worth another round. The behavior you see is already correct, and the extra commands cost four seconds and change nothing. I would put it in, since the line is about to be committed and the next fresh session tests it for free.

180:## Agent-files version
181-
182-The agent-files set has a version of its own, apart from the artifact's, so which set an adopter
183-carries is read from a listing rather than a diff, and an `agent-files` title has a token that is
184-unique by construction ([Project-declared types](prose.md#project-declared-types),
185-[why](rationale.md#agent-files-version)).
186-
187-- **Record**: an empty file, `agent-data/agent-files-vX.Y.Z{-suffix}`, the version its name. `ls
188-  agent-data` shows it without a read, a bump is a rename, and
189-  `git log --diff-filter=A -- 'agent-data/agent-files-v*'` lists every version beside the commit
190-  that introduced it.
191-- **Spelling**: `vX.Y.Z` everywhere the agent-files version is written, the file name, an
192-  `agent-files` title, and vc-x1's output, so `agent-files v0.1.0` reads the same in all three. The
193-  `v` is the name-plus-version pair as cargo prints it (`bar v1.0.0`), and a tool's own banner stays
194-  bare (`vc-x1 0.82.0`), so a `v` number is the set's and a bare one the artifact's.
195-- **Proposals bump, adoptions copy**: a proposal cycle bumps it at the opening, advancing per
196-  [Advancing X.Y.Z](#advancing-xyz-patch-by-default), and its rungs walk the [Suffix
197-  scheme](#suffix-scheme) beside the artifact's version, `-0`, `-1`, then bare at the close-out, so
198-  a set copied from a draft bookmark says on its face that it is unfinished. An adoption copies the
199-  source's bare file and bumps nothing.
200-- **Agreed**: the payload's number is the family's agreed version. An adopter ahead of it is
201-  proposing, one behind has not re-synced, and two proposers claiming one number are settled by the
202-  maintainer at convergence, the loser re-proposing under the next.
203-- **Which digit**: tend toward the patch digit, kept to one digit and rolled over into the minor.
204-  We think the minor stays within two digits and major increments when the family decides.

content.text:
My thought is that this should not be a proposal yet, and if it is one, v0.2.8 is already taken.

**Why not a proposal as it stands**
- **The change is in `custom.md`, which is the project layer.** A proposal is a change meant for the set, and [Changing the agent-files](AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files) says such a rule goes into the agent-file it belongs to, never held in `custom.md`. For the lock that is `AGENTS.md > Acquaint`, with its why in `rationale.md`.
- **The `TODO.md` entry records the opposite call.** It says "an edit of our own `custom.md` and no `agent-files` proposal, wink's call, still its own commit." You can change that, but then the line should move.
- **It is not ready for other adopters.** Two cases are untested (the holder dying with its session, a reacquaint in the session that holds the lock), and `flock` is a Linux tool that macOS does not ship. The better moment to propose is when `vc-x1` owns the lock and the rule can name a `vc-x1` command.

**The number, if you do propose it**
- The set is at v0.2.7 here (`agent-data/agent-files-v0.2.7`).
- v0.2.8 is claimed by the parked commit on `agent-filesproposal-v028`, which is published and carries the number in its title and bookmark name. It also happens to touch `custom.md`.
- Two commits titled `agent-files(proposal): v0.2.8` would break the rule that the title's version token is unique. So either this takes v0.2.8 and the parked one is renumbered to v0.2.9 when it resumes (it is due a rebase and rewrite anyway), or this takes v0.2.9 and `main` skips a number until the parked one lands.
- Of those two I would take v0.2.8 here and renumber the parked one, since a gap on `main` reads as a missing version.

**What I recommend**
Commit it now as a plain single-step cycle on its own bookmark, with an ordinary title such as `docs: a session takes the workspace lock at acquaint`, and no agent-files version bump. Promote it to a proposal in the cycle that adds `.vc-x1-running`, moving the rule into `AGENTS.md` then.

The plain version: it is a rule for this project only so far, so it does not need a set version; and if you want it to be one for everyone, the number 0.2.8 already has an owner.

content.content:
150	### Cycle shape
151	
152	Single-step or multi-step is decided at the opening and fixed by the cycle's first push, with the
153	one coordinated exception below ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycle-shape)). Before that push the
154	In Progress block may be rewritten to either shape. After it:
155	
156	- A single-step cycle is one commit, made by one push, carrying the opening's duties, the work, and
157	  the close-out's duties, titled with the bare cycle title in both repos. When the work turns out to
158	  need more steps, two choices, since the bookmark is still a draft:
159	  - land the commit as it is and run the additional work as one or more further cycles
160	  - turn the commit into the opening: amend its version-of-record to the `-0` form, re-title it with
161	    " opening" as a coordinated re-describe that keeps the `ochid:` trailer ([No re-describe without
162	    coordinating](agent-data/jj.md#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer)), and
163	    complete the cycle as multi-step.
164	- A multi-step cycle is a ladder and lands as a trapezoid or kept separate, never squashed: every
165	  rung's `ochid:` trailer is a change id, and a squash discards all but one. A ladder that shrinks
166	  to one rung still closes as a ladder, since its opening already pushed.
167	
168	### Unplanned work
169	
170	Work that arrives while a cycle runs goes one of two ways, and the user picks which
171	([why](agent-data/rationale.md#unplanned-work)):
172	
173	- A rung inserted into the ladder, usually when it is inside the cycle's subject or blocks it.
174	- A `## Todo` or `## Waiting` entry, run as its own cycle later.
175	
176	A rung inserted while the working copy already holds the next rung's edits sets those edits aside
177	as a patch first, so the inserted rung's commit carries its own change alone, and they return once
178	it has pushed.
179	
180	### Cycle-record
181	
182	A cycle's record is its `TODO.md > ## In Progress` block and nothing else, the cycle-record
183	([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycle-record)).
184	
185	- Items: title, problem, solution, acceptance check, deliberation, and the ladder heading its rung
186	  subsections, all provisional until close-out ([The In Progress
187	  block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block)).
188	- Life: written at the opening, revised as rungs land, finalized by the closing commit, which moves
189	  it whole to `## Closed` (a single-step cycle's one commit writes it there directly), deleted by
190	  the next opening.
191	  - `## In Progress` reads `_No cycle currently in progress._` between cycles.
192	  - The closing commit's tree carries the final form, and the file never grows.
193	- After that jj holds it: `git log --grep "<cycle title>"` finds the commits, on the title the
194	  pushed bookends carry when a rename came mid-cycle, and the landmark on `main` (the trapezoid
195	  merge, or the single-step commit) holds the finished block in its `TODO.md > ## Closed`.
196	- No backfill: a rung carries no `[[N]]` placeholder, no SHA, and no version.
197	- Never amended: a late finding about a closed cycle is recorded where it is found, citing the
198	  landmark.
199	- Design findings that must outlive the cycle go into a `notes/` file by the rung that made them,
200	  never left in the block.
201	- Frozen history: `notes/chores/` and `notes/done.md` are never appended, still linked.
202	
203	### Opening
204	
205	The cycle's first commit, when it needs setup (a lightweight cycle starts at its first commit, which
206	then carries step 1). A single-step cycle does all of it in its one commit, after step 1 ([Cycle
207	shape](#cycle-shape)). Before that commit ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#opening)):
208	
209	1. Bookmark: create and publish the cycle's bookmark, a push that needs approval.
210	2. Waiting: check each `## Waiting` entry's condition, and promote what is met into `## Todo` at
211	   the rank it names.
212	3. In Progress block: delete whatever `## Closed` holds, then move the chosen `## Todo` entry into
213	   `## In Progress`, shaped as [The In Progress block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block)
214	   says, the specimen in [cycle-model.md](agent-data/cycle-model.md).
215	4. Bump: bump the version-of-record to the opening's version ([Suffix
216	   scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)), and the agent-files version with it when the
217	   cycle is an `agent-files` proposal ([Agent-files
218	   version](agent-data/versioning.md#agent-files-version)).
219	5. Rename: when the built artifact has consumers, rename `<name>` to `<name>-dev` ([Dev artifact
220	   name](agent-data/versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)). Land restores it.
221	
222	Rungs are named, not numbered ([Steps are named, not numbered][snn]), and a multi-step cycle's
223	bookends are the cycle title plus " opening" and " closing" ([Cycle bookend titles][cbt]).
224	
225	### The per-rung flow
226	
227	Every commit (opening, each rung between, closing) goes through these steps, read from here
228	immediately before acting ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#the-per-rung-flow)):
229	
230	1. Mark current: mark the rung `(current)` in `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, as the first edit.
231	2. Bump: bump the version-of-record to this commit's version ([Suffix
232	   scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)), the agent-files version beside it in an
233	   `agent-files` proposal cycle.
234	3. Work: do the work. On any deviation from the agreed plan, or any question, stop ([Stop and
235	   ask](#stop-and-ask)).
236	4. Rung subsection: write what this rung changed, conceptually, into its subsection under the
237	   ladder. The rung stays `(current)` until step 7.
238	5. Validate: `vc-x1 validate` before every review, doc-only commits included. The full run rewrites

### Cycle shape

Single-step or multi-step is decided at the opening and fixed by the cycle's first push, with the
one coordinated exception below ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycle-shape)). Before that push the
In Progress block may be rewritten to either shape. After it:

- A single-step cycle is one commit, made by one push, carrying the opening's duties, the work, and
  the close-out's duties, titled with the bare cycle title in both repos. When the work turns out to
  need more steps, two choices, since the bookmark is still a draft:
  - land the commit as it is and run the additional work as one or more further cycles
  - turn the commit into the opening: amend its version-of-record to the `-0` form, re-title it with
    " opening" as a coordinated re-describe that keeps the `ochid:` trailer ([No re-describe without
    coordinating](agent-data/jj.md#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer)), and
    complete the cycle as multi-step.
- A multi-step cycle is a ladder and lands as a trapezoid or kept separate, never squashed: every
  rung's `ochid:` trailer is a change id, and a squash discards all but one. A ladder that shrinks
  to one rung still closes as a ladder, since its opening already pushed.

### Unplanned work

Work that arrives while a cycle runs goes one of two ways, and the user picks which
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#unplanned-work)):

- A rung inserted into the ladder, usually when it is inside the cycle's subject or blocks it.
- A `## Todo` or `## Waiting` entry, run as its own cycle later.

A rung inserted while the working copy already holds the next rung's edits sets those edits aside
as a patch first, so the inserted rung's commit carries its own change alone, and they return once
it has pushed.

### Cycle-record

A cycle's record is its `TODO.md > ## In Progress` block and nothing else, the cycle-record
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#cycle-record)).

- Items: title, problem, solution, acceptance check, deliberation, and the ladder heading its rung
  subsections, all provisional until close-out ([The In Progress
  block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block)).
- Life: written at the opening, revised as rungs land, finalized by the closing commit, which moves
  it whole to `## Closed` (a single-step cycle's one commit writes it there directly), deleted by
  the next opening.
  - `## In Progress` reads `_No cycle currently in progress._` between cycles.
  - The closing commit's tree carries the final form, and the file never grows.
- After that jj holds it: `git log --grep "<cycle title>"` finds the commits, on the title the
  pushed bookends carry when a rename came mid-cycle, and the landmark on `main` (the trapezoid
  merge, or the single-step commit) holds the finished block in its `TODO.md > ## Closed`.
- No backfill: a rung carries no `[[N]]` placeholder, no SHA, and no version.
- Never amended: a late finding about a closed cycle is recorded where it is found, citing the
  landmark.
- Design findings that must outlive the cycle go into a `notes/` file by the rung that made them,
  never left in the block.
- Frozen history: `notes/chores/` and `notes/done.md` are never appended, still linked.

### Opening

The cycle's first commit, when it needs setup (a lightweight cycle starts at its first commit, which
then carries step 1). A single-step cycle does all of it in its one commit, after step 1 ([Cycle
shape](#cycle-shape)). Before that commit ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#opening)):

1. Bookmark: create and publish the cycle's bookmark, a push that needs approval.
2. Waiting: check each `## Waiting` entry's condition, and promote what is met into `## Todo` at
   the rank it names.
3. In Progress block: delete whatever `## Closed` holds, then move the chosen `## Todo` entry into
   `## In Progress`, shaped as [The In Progress block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block)
   says, the specimen in [cycle-model.md](agent-data/cycle-model.md).
4. Bump: bump the version-of-record to the opening's version ([Suffix
   scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)), and the agent-files version with it when the
   cycle is an `agent-files` proposal ([Agent-files
   version](agent-data/versioning.md#agent-files-version)).
5. Rename: when the built artifact has consumers, rename `<name>` to `<name>-dev` ([Dev artifact
   name](agent-data/versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)). Land restores it.

Rungs are named, not numbered ([Steps are named, not numbered][snn]), and a multi-step cycle's
bookends are the cycle title plus " opening" and " closing" ([Cycle bookend titles][cbt]).

### The per-rung flow

Every commit (opening, each rung between, closing) goes through these steps, read from here
immediately before acting ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#the-per-rung-flow)):

1. Mark current: mark the rung `(current)` in `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, as the first edit.
2. Bump: bump the version-of-record to this commit's version ([Suffix
   scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)), the agent-files version beside it in an
   `agent-files` proposal cycle.
3. Work: do the work. On any deviation from the agreed plan, or any question, stop ([Stop and
   ask](#stop-and-ask)).
4. Rung subsection: write what this rung changed, conceptually, into its subsection under the
   ladder. The rung stays `(current)` until step 7.
5. Validate: `vc-x1 validate` before every review, doc-only commits included. The full run rewrites
   files (`cargo fmt`), so use `--fast` while a review iterates.
6. Work review: stop before writing any description and say "please review", as its own message with
   no title or body. Iterate until the user says "continue" / "go". The review is of the
   working-copy diff ([jj basics](agent-data/jj.md#jj-basics)).
7. Flip and describe: flip `(current)` to `(done)` the moment "done" is true, then write the
   description in [Commit-body form](agent-data/prose.md#commit-body-form), read from the file first
   with its specimen, [commit-model.md](agent-data/commit-model.md) ([Commit
   description](#commit-description)).
8. Description review: show the title + body and stop. Ask permission to commit and push without
   spelling out the invocation. The go covers the push only when it says so.
9. Commit + push: on the go, `vc-x1 push <bookmark> --title "..." --body "..."` ([Committing vs
   pushing](#committing-vs-pushing)), then [At rest](#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push).

### Committing vs pushing

A cycle rung is committed *by* `vc-x1 push`, never pre-committed with `jj commit`
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#committing-vs-pushing)). "Commit", "push",
and "commit + push" all mean `vc-x1 push`. A bare `jj commit` is asked for by name and is for local
saves and [local ladder](#local-ladders) intermediates. What push does is in [vc-x1 push][vpush].

### Commit description

111	## vc-x1 push: what it does and does not do
112	
113	`vc-x1 push <bookmark> --yes --title "..." --body "..."` commits both repos with the approved title
114	and body (`--yes` because push's gates need a tty the agent sandbox lacks, and the user's approval
115	of the shown title and body already covers them), stamps each new commit's `ochid:` trailer
116	([above](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), pushes the work bookmark, and squash-pushes the agent
117	repo's `main`. Three behaviors to keep in mind:
118	
119	- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 runs no build or tests. Validation is the per-rung
120	  flow's job, run *before* the push. The one check that remains is `push-work` verifying the
121	  bookmark's remote refs are tracked.
122	- **Rerunning is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume: every stage no-ops when its work is
123	  already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed. If push exits after `push-work` but before
124	  the agent-repo publish, `vc-x1 squash-push -R <agent-dir>` by hand is the rest of it.
125	- **`ochid:` trailers are stamped by push** ([No hand-written
126	  trailers](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), never hand-written into `--title` or `--body`.
127	- **The agent-repo is a linear journal.**
128	  - One push is one agent-repo commit on its `main`, paired with the work-repo commit, whatever
129	    bookmark the work-repo is on.
130	  - Never create an agent-repo bookmark mirroring a work-repo one: it steers session pushes at
131	    the wrong remote ref.
132	- **Squash-push again if `@` is non-empty** after a pass.
133	  - The agent keeps writing session data while the command runs, so its own record lands after
134	    the squash.
135	  - Session data is append-only, so a re-run never conflicts.
136	  - A single pass is never guaranteed to leave `@` empty.
137	
138	A late work-repo tweak after the push (a forgotten edit) needs `jj squash --ignore-immutable` and a
139	re-push, which is a remote rewrite and takes approval like any push.
140	
141	## Re-describing: coordinate first, and keep the trailer
142	
143	**Never `jj describe` a commit that is already published or already carries trailers without
144	coordinating with everyone involved first**
145	([why](rationale.md#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer)). It is a history rewrite,
146	and it silently drops the cross-repo link. Describing a fresh local commit that has never been
147	described and carries no trailers is authoring a message rather than rewriting one, and is not
148	covered. That is a [local
149	ladder](../AGENTS.md#local-ladders)'s scratch describe.
150	
151	When a re-describe is agreed, copy any `ochid:` trailers into the new body by hand (the "don't
152	hand-write trailers" rule covers push authoring a message from scratch, not preserving one already
153	stamped). Hit at a coordinated amend (2026-07-29), where the trailer survived only that way.
154	`vc-x1 fix-desc` repairs a dropped one by title match.
155	
156	## Cycle bookmarks: create and land
157	
158	The mechanics behind [Cycles run on a bookmark](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark). That section
159	holds the rule and when it applies, and this one holds the commands
160	([why](rationale.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)).
161	
162	**Create**, at the cycle's opening, with the bookmark named by the cycle title's slug (the anchor
163	algorithm in [Markdown anchor links](notes.md#markdown-anchor-links), so the block's title heading
164	and the bookmark derive from one bare title):
165	
166	- `jj git push --named <bookmark>=@- -R .` is the common case: it creates the bookmark at the last
167	  committed change and publishes it in one invocation.
168	- Any other revision works as the `=<rev>` right-hand side. When `<rev>` is not `@-`, follow with
169	  `jj new <rev> -R .` so the working copy actually sits on the new line. Otherwise the bookmark
170	  exists and the next commit lands somewhere else.
171	- `jj bookmark set <bookmark> -r <rev> -R .` creates it without publishing, for a line that is not
172	  ready to be seen.
173	
174	**Land**, once the close-out is approved: the sequence that makes the cycle permanent. Every
175	`jj git push` in it is a push under [Approval per push](../AGENTS.md#before-any-push) and [Hard
176	stop after the final push](../AGENTS.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push), its own approval, the
177	closing words before the final invocation, silence after ([At
178	rest](../AGENTS.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push)):
179	
180	1. Restore the plain name, when the project renamed ([Dev artifact
181	   name](versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)): rename `<name>-dev` back to `<name>` in the manifest,
182	   `vc-x1 validate --fast` so the lockfile follows, and `jj squash` folds the edit into the closing
183	   (`@` sits directly above it).
184	2. Reshape per the recorded choice: trapezoid runs the [recipe below](#trapezoid-close-out-recipe),
185	   keep separate needs nothing. A single-step cycle has no choice recorded and its one commit lands
186	   as it is.
187	3. Fast-forward: `jj bookmark set main -r <closeout> -R .`, then `jj git push --bookmark main -R .`.
188	   This push publishes the reshaped commit, so the topic bookmark itself is never re-pushed.
189	4. Install: promote the artifact from `main`, the cycle's last act, run when nothing can enter the
190	   cycle anymore.
191	5. Delete the bookmark, locally and remotely: `jj bookmark delete <bookmark>`, then
192	   `jj git push --bookmark <bookmark>` ([Bookmark per
193	   cycle](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)). The long-lived case below gets the same
194	   disposal once fully merged.
195	
196	- The fast-forward needs no `--allow-backwards`. Needing it means the bookmark is not a descendant
197	  of `main`, and the situation wants a look, not a flag.
198	- Landing is the moment the cycle's commits become permanent. No record cites their SHAs
199	  ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)): the landed commits are the record.
200	
201	**Reshape**, while the bookmark is a draft ([Cycles run on a
202	bookmark](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)):
203	
204	- **Amend content, never re-describe.** Editing `TODO.md` in a rung and amending is not a
205	  `jj describe`, so [No re-describe without
206	  coordinating](#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer) stays intact.
207	- **Then force-push the bookmark**, under the same approval as any other push.
208	- **Exceptions**, named and moved past: the bookmark has already landed, another branch is stacked
209	  on it, or the ladder is long and only a trailing snapshot disagrees.

stop after the final push](../AGENTS.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push), its own approval, the
closing words before the final invocation, silence after ([At
rest](../AGENTS.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push)):

1. Restore the plain name, when the project renamed ([Dev artifact
   name](versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)): rename `<name>-dev` back to `<name>` in the manifest,
   `vc-x1 validate --fast` so the lockfile follows, and `jj squash` folds the edit into the closing
   (`@` sits directly above it).
2. Reshape per the recorded choice: trapezoid runs the [recipe below](#trapezoid-close-out-recipe),
   keep separate needs nothing. A single-step cycle has no choice recorded and its one commit lands
   as it is.
3. Fast-forward: `jj bookmark set main -r <closeout> -R .`, then `jj git push --bookmark main -R .`.
   This push publishes the reshaped commit, so the topic bookmark itself is never re-pushed.
4. Install: promote the artifact from `main`, the cycle's last act, run when nothing can enter the
   cycle anymore.
5. Delete the bookmark, locally and remotely: `jj bookmark delete <bookmark>`, then
   `jj git push --bookmark <bookmark>` ([Bookmark per
   cycle](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)). The long-lived case below gets the same
   disposal once fully merged.

- The fast-forward needs no `--allow-backwards`. Needing it means the bookmark is not a descendant
  of `main`, and the situation wants a look, not a flag.
- Landing is the moment the cycle's commits become permanent. No record cites their SHAs
  ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)): the landed commits are the record.

**Reshape**, while the bookmark is a draft ([Cycles run on a
bookmark](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)):

- **Amend content, never re-describe.** Editing `TODO.md` in a rung and amending is not a
  `jj describe`, so [No re-describe without
  coordinating](#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer) stays intact.
- **Then force-push the bookmark**, under the same approval as any other push.
- **Exceptions**, named and moved past: the bookmark has already landed, another branch is stacked
  on it, or the ladder is long and only a trailing snapshot disagrees.

70	  record, `_None._` by default, written before a restart or a loss of context, and reset by the
71	  agent that reads it, after filing each fact into its home or keeping the bullet whose fact has

74	- `## Waiting`: important work that cannot start yet. Each entry names what it waits on and its
75	  rank once unblocked, and every opening checks the conditions.
76	- `## Todo`: entries in priority order, the first highest. The long-tail backlog is in
77	  [todo-backlog.md](../notes/todo-backlog.md).
78	- `## Ideas`: unranked.
79	- `## Bugs`: a pointer to [bugs.md](../notes/bugs.md).
80	- `## Closed`: the last cycle's finished record.
81	- `# References`: the file-local reference definitions, the file's last section ([Reference
82	  numbering](#reference-numbering)).
83	
84	Every adopter has one `TODO.md` of this shape. It is not an agent-file, since its content is the
85	project's record, and the payload ships it as a skeleton: `## In Progress` reading
86	`_No cycle currently in progress._`, the other sections empty.
87	
88	An entry is a `###` heading, its title, followed by its text. Priority is file order, the first
89	entry the highest, and reprioritizing is moving the entry. The title is unique within its file and
90	is the entry's anchor, so a citation is a link, `[title](TODO.md#<slug>)`, that the anchor check
91	verifies ([Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) for the text). Entries carry no number: a rank number
92	renumbers on every move and every citation that holds one goes stale, which is why the numbered
93	form was retired (2026-08-27). An entry's sub-entries, when it groups several, are bullets with a
94	bold title, cited by the bold text.
95	
96	Example shape:
97	
98	```
99	## Todo
100	
101	### Add new feature X
102	
103	The feature, in a sentence or two ([details](features.md#feature-x)).
104	
105	### Fix bug Y
106	
107	What is wrong and where [[1]].
108	
109	[1]: bugs.md#bug-y
110	```
111	
112	## The In Progress block
113	
114	A cycle's record, `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, written at the opening
115	([Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), finalized and moved to `## Closed` by the closing commit, and
116	deleted by the next opening ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)). The picked-up `## Todo`
117	item is moved here (never copied) and becomes the cycle-record's **provisional items**, all
118	required, all revised as rungs land. The title is a heading one level below `## In Progress` and the
119	other five are headings one level below the title (a plain cycle: `###` title, `####` items, and
120	under a program heading, each one deeper):
121	
122	- **title**, the cycle's name, what `git log --grep` finds it by
123	- **problem statement**: what is wrong, a sentence or two
124	- **solution statement**: what will be done about it, broad. Provisional, and the close-out's commit
125	  body carries the final one
126	- **acceptance check**: the measure of "are you finished?", specific enough that a reader can run
127	  it. Not the per-commit validation, which asks whether the artifact still works. A changed check is
128	  one of the things the deliberation exists to justify
129	- **deliberation**: how the other five were decided, one bullet per decision. The bullet's lead
130	  names the decision and its sentence states it, and the sub-bullets carry the reasons, the
131	  alternatives weighed, and the costs accepted, so a reader can skim the decisions and read the
132	  reasons only where they doubt one. `_None._` when there was nothing to deliberate, which is a real
133	  answer
134	- **ladder**: one rung per step, `- [<title>][M]` plus `(current)` / `(done)`, with `[M]: #<slug>`
135	  in the file's `# References`. The markers stay when the block moves to `## Closed`. `<title>` is
136	  the rung's commit title, `<type>: <desc>` per
137	  [Conventional-commit shape](prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit), so a moved
138	  `## Todo` entry is retitled. The closing rung, `<cycle title> closing`, is linked like the rest
139	
140	The ladder heads the **rung subsections**, one per rung under it, the closing included, headed by
141	the rung's exact title, so the ladder is their index. Each opens at laddering with an abstract-sized
142	intent statement (the rung's problem and solution in a sentence or two) and completes at the rung's
143	landing with the conceptual delta: design points, consequences, deferrals, never a restatement of
144	the landed commit body. The closing rung's opens with the stub "Closing out the cycle." and
145	completes at close-out with what closing taught, in problem/solution form, or `_None._`.
146	
147	A rung is `- [<title>][M] (marker)` and carries no detail beyond that: the title links to the rung's
148	subsection. A step is identified by its title (prose.md's [Steps are named, not
149	numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)), so a title carries no number, no version, and no
150	SHA. The version-of-record still bumps for every rung and its suffix still encodes the stage, but
151	that encoding belongs to the manifest and appears nowhere in prose.
152	
153	A single-step cycle's ladder is one unlinked rung, `- <cycle title> (marker)`, with no subsection
154	under it: a subsection headed by the title would collide with the title heading's anchor ([Cycle
155	shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).
156	
157	The block is the cycle's only record. A design finding that must outlive the cycle goes into a
158	`notes/` file by the rung that made it ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
159	
160	## Frozen history: chores and done
161	
162	`notes/chores/chores-NN.md` and `notes/done.md` are the records of cycles that ran before the
163	cycle-record became `TODO.md > ## In Progress` alone ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).

cycle, mid-run, with its opening landed and its first work rung current. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [The In Progress block](notes.md#the-in-progress-block).

  unlinked rung with the bare title, and there are no rung subsections under it ([Cycle

## In Progress

### refactor: extract config loader

#### Problem

Config parsing lives inside the CLI entry point, so every subcommand that wants a setting reaches
through `main` for it, and a test cannot load a config without building the CLI.

#### Solution

Move config loading into its own module with a single `load` entry point that the CLI and the tests
call alike.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a new test that loads a config from a fixture file without touching `main`,
and `vc-x1 config --validate` reports the same findings as before the move.

#### Deliberation

- one work rung, not two: the parser and the loader were going to be split first and moved second,
  but the move is what forces the split, so doing them together is fewer edits
- the acceptance check compares `config --validate` output rather than asserting on internals, so a
  later rename inside the module does not invalidate it

#### Ladder

- [refactor: extract config loader opening][1] (done)
- [refactor: split loader from parser][2] (current)
- [refactor: extract config loader closing][3]

##### refactor: extract config loader opening

The cycle's setup commit: create and publish the bookmark, delete `## Closed`'s contents, move the
Todo entry into this block, and bump the version-of-record.

##### refactor: split loader from parser

Loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load without parsing and a test cannot parse
without a file on disk.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config/loader.rs` finds and reads the file, returning the text and its path, so a caller that
    only wants to know which file was read stops here.
  - `config/parser.rs` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands it a string and never
    touches the filesystem.
    - the error type stays shared for now, since splitting it would change the messages
      `config --validate` prints and the acceptance check compares them
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field access moves behind the module
    boundary and the CLI no longer knows the file's shape.

##### refactor: extract config loader closing

Closing out the cycle.

3	The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
4	its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the

9	
10	### docs: update single-step cycle add zCLOSED.md
11	
12	(wink + agent, 2026-10-11) A session of planning left `TODO.md` holding a day of decisions as
13	uncommitted edits, with no cycle to carry them: what `vc-x1 delete` and `vc-x1 rename` are to do,
14	the order `init` is fixed in, and two faults the day turned up, commits no command reports and a
15	checker that reports a working link as broken. Carrying them became a trial of how a single-step
16	cycle runs and of where the last record is kept, and the trial is what the cycle is named for.
17	
18	#### Deliberation
19	
20	- The cycle is single-step, wink's call: the edits were made in conversation, entry by entry.
21	- The cycle is a trial of a new shape for a single-step cycle, wink's call at the work review of
22	  the one-commit form, before any `vc-x1 push`: two stages, the work and the closing, each
23	  validated, reviewed, and pushed, so a single-step cycle and a multi-step one run alike.
24	  - The first stage carries the opening's duties and the work, under the dev name at the `-1`
25	    suffix, the record in `## In Progress`.
26	  - The closing runs the acceptance check against the pushed work, sets the bare version, and
27	    moves the block to this file.
28	  - The work-repo carries one commit and the agent-repo two, wink's call at the closing's
29	    review. The closing is folded into the pushed work commit, which keeps its change id, and
30	    the second agent-repo commit's trailer names that same commit.
31	    - The work commit carries two `ochid:` trailers, one for each agent-repo commit.
32	    - Two work commits squashed at Land would have left one agent-repo commit naming a change id
33	      that no longer exists, the reason a ladder is never squashed.
34	    - It was done by hand: a `jj squash`, a `jj describe` that kept the first trailer and added
35	      the second, written by hand, and then `vc-x1 push`, which skips an empty work side and
36	      stamps the agent-repo commit with the existing work commit's id.
37	    - It is a re-describe of a published commit, coordinated with wink, and it bends [No
38	      hand-written trailers](agent-data/jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers) for the one
39	      trailer.
40	    - `vc-x1 validate-desc` and `fix-desc` read the last trailer alone. Both, and a `push
41	      --amend` that does the fold, are Todo entries written by this closing.
42	  - The cycle was renamed at the closing, wink's call: it opened as "docs: Todo plans init,
43	    delete, and rename", which names the occasion and not what was done.
44	    - The work commit is re-titled with the fold. The first agent-repo commit keeps the old
45	      title, that repo being a journal of what was said at the time, and the bookmark keeps the
46	      old name until Land deletes it.
47	  - The last cycle's record stays readable until this one's closing replaces it, wink's call at
48	    the second work review, where the opening would have deleted it. There is then always a
49	    finished record, and the opening's diff is its own cycle alone. Wink means it for a
50	    multi-step cycle too.
51	    - It was first tried as two blocks in `zDOING.md`, the old one left under `## Closed`. They
52	      shared the file's reference definitions, so the new block's had to number on from the
53	      old one's, and they repeated the item headings, Deliberation, Solution, Acceptance check,
54	      and Ladder, which `vc-x1 validate-anchors` reported as four duplicate anchors.
55	    - A list of references inside each block was weighed and left: a definition is the file's
56	      wherever it is written, so two blocks cannot both number from 1. A rung's title as its
57	      label would have answered that and not the headings.
58	    - A file of its own, wink's idea, answers both: `zCLOSED.md` holds the last record and its
59	      references, each file numbers from 1, and the closing replaces that file's block whole.
60	      Its cost is a third file beside `zDOING.md` and `TODO.md`.

# Closed: the last cycle's record

The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the
last record stays here until the next one is finished. Earlier cycles are in each landmark
commit's copy of the record.

### docs: update single-step cycle add zCLOSED.md

uncommitted edits, with no cycle to carry them: what `vc-x1 delete` and `vc-x1 rename` are to do,
the order `init` is fixed in, and two faults the day turned up, commits no command reports and a

33	## Advancing X.Y.Z: patch by default
34	
35	Which of the three numbers moves is not a classification problem
36	([why](rationale.md#advancing-xyz-patch-by-default)): **patch by default, minor by the user's call,
37	major by the project's promise.**
38	
39	- **Patch by default**: every cycle advances `Z`, whatever it touched. Code or docs, large or small,
40	  none of it matters, so the choice costs no deliberation.
41	- **Minor is deliberate and rare**: the user names it at a cycle's opening when the change deserves
42	  a visible marker in the history, and the agent never infers it from a change's content or size.
43	- **Major is a project's own call**, since what `X` promises depends on the artifact and its users.
44	  A project that makes that promise records it as its local edit of this rule, and absent one the
45	  default above governs.
46	
47	## Grammar and storage
48	
49	One spelling everywhere the version is written:
50	
51	```
52	<public>[-<suffix>]
53	```
54	
55	- `<public>`: `X.Y.Z`, integers.
56	- `<suffix>`: dot-separated identifiers, each ASCII letters or digits: usually integers (`3`, `3.1`,
57	  `3.1.0`), with an alphanumeric id (`3.hotfix`) allowed sparingly.
58	- **Exactly one `-` in the whole version**, the one that opens the suffix: never a dash inside the
59	  suffix, never a `+` in this spelling. This is the portability invariant that makes the version
60	  storable in every medium below ([why](rationale.md#grammar-and-storage)).
61	- **`v` is a display prefix, not part of the version**: conversation and reports may write
62	  `v0.78.0-3.1` for scannability, while manifests store the bare form. (PEP 440 ignores a leading
63	  `v`. Cargo rejects one.)
64	
65	Storage is a per-medium remap of that one spelling:
66	
67	- **SemVer mediums** (Rust/Cargo): store verbatim. The suffix rides in the prerelease slot, valid at
68	  any dot depth.
69	- **PEP 440 mediums** (Python): remap the single `-` to `+`: `0.78.0-3.1` -> `0.78.0+3.1`.
70	  Mechanical and bijective because there is exactly one dash to find.
71	- **Other mediums**: verbatim if the format allows the one `-`, else the `+` remap. A new medium
72	  adds its case to [Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record).
73	
74	Two reservations keep the remap sound:
75	
76	- **The stored version identifies but does not order.** SemVer sorts a suffixed version *before* its
77	  bare release (matching cycle semantics: rungs precede close-out), while PEP 440 sorts the remapped
78	  form *after* it, and reinterprets a lone `-N` as a post-release. Opposite directions, so no
79	  cross-medium logic may compare stored versions. Ordering truth lives in the ladder and git
80	  history. Comparing the public triple alone (e.g. a version gate) is unaffected.
81	- **`+` is reserved** for the PEP 440 remap: no SemVer build-metadata use in Rust repos even though
82	  Cargo allows it, since spending `+` there breaks the bijection with the Python spelling. A repo
83	  that truly needs it declares the deviation in its `custom.md`.
84	
85	## Recording the version-of-record
86	
87	Where the version-of-record lives, how it's stored and surfaced, and how often it changes. Pick the
88	case that fits your medium:
89	
90	- **Manifest**, where the version-of-record is stored:
91	  - if Rust, `Cargo.toml` `[package].version`
92	  - if Python, `pyproject.toml` `[project].version` (or the committed config it's sourced from)
93	  - otherwise wherever the medium records it (a generic `version.toml`, a book's frontmatter, ...).
94	    Add the case as needed
95	- **Notation**, how the `-` form is stored. See [Grammar and storage](#grammar-and-storage):
96	  - if the format allows `-` (TOML `version.toml`, `Cargo.toml`), store it verbatim
97	  - if it bars `-` (PEP 440's local segment, e.g. a Python project), remap to `+`, so `0.3.0-5.3.0`
98	    becomes `0.3.0+5.3.0`: same version, just the stored spelling
99	- **Reporter**, how a built artifact surfaces the version-of-record:
100	  - if a CLI app, `<cli-app> -V`
101	  - if a TUI/GUI, add to Help/About or display on the title
102	- **Cadence**, how often to bump: see [Unique per
103	  commit](#unique-per-commit-preference-not-requirement). This project follows the per-commit
104	  preference.
105	
106	## Dev artifact name
107	
108	When other projects consume the built artifact (e.g. the installed CLI) while this repo is under
109	active development, the dev build installs under a separate name so a mid-cycle install never
110	clobbers the binary consumers are running:
111	
112	- **Name**: the manifest's package name carries a `-dev` suffix (`<name>` -> `<name>-dev`). If Rust,
113	  `[package].name`, so the per-commit flow's `cargo install` produces `<name>-dev` and leaves plain
114	  `<name>` untouched.
115	- **Constant, not per-step**: the step already lives in the version-of-record (`<name>-dev -V`
116	  reports the exact rung). A per-step name would churn the manifest every commit and litter the
117	  install dir with stale binaries.
118	- **Promotion**: plain `<name>` updates only by an explicit act: a separate clone built at the
119	  chosen commit with the plain name (or a copy of the dev binary), never by the per-commit flow's
120	  install.
121	
122	**Single-name variant**: a repo striving to release makes the package name the binary's name, plain
123	`<name>` on `main` only:
124	
125	- **The opening renames**: its bump sets `<name>-dev` beside the suffixed version, and every rung
126	  and the closing build under the dev name, the closing over the bare version.
127	- **Land restores**: the rename back to `<name>` is Land's act, so the stable name is only ever
128	  installed from what `main` will carry.
129	- **A build script guards the pairing** on every cargo verb: a suffixed version under the stable
130	  name fails the build, so no mid-cycle install can clobber the consumers' binary.
131	
132	## Unique per commit (preference, not requirement)
133	
134	Our general notion is that the version-of-record should change on **every commit**, so a built or
135	running artifact identifies the exact commit it came from.
136	
137	- This is a preference, **not** a hard requirement. A project following the cycle protocol may bump
138	  less often: once per cycle, only at release, and so on. Record the choice in [Recording the
139	  version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record) if it differs.
140	- It is achievable because the cycle's versions (below) are **pre-assignable**, unlike the git SHA,
141	  which a commit cannot contain.
142	
143	## Suffix scheme
144	
145	The cycle (opening -> commits -> closing, per the [Cycle protocol](../AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol))
146	encodes each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a
147	Preparation**.
148	
149	This is the manifest's own spelling, read by whoever inspects `Cargo.toml` or `-V` output. It is not
150	a name for a step: a step is identified by its title, and an in-flight ladder rung carries neither a
151	number nor a version (see [Steps are named, not numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)).
152	The identifiers below count commits within a phase, and nothing dereferences one.
153	
154	- `X.Y.Z-0`: Preparation
155	- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, ...: the commits between
156	- `X.Y.Z`: Close-out (bare version, no suffix)
157	
158	**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle, with no ladder and no setup commit, skips `-0` and
159	starts at `-1` (its first commit). A single-step cycle is one commit, the Close-out, and carries the
160	bare `X.Y.Z` ([Cycle shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle
161	needing no Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that grows a Preparation later adds the `0`
162	step without renumbering siblings.
163	
164	Disambiguation:
165	
166	- `-10`: commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a Preparation.
167	- `-1.0`: Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final identifier `0`).
168	
169	**Nesting.** Sub-cycles append another level, recursively:
170	
171	- `X.Y.Z-3.0`: Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle
172	- `X.Y.Z-3.1`, `X.Y.Z-3.2`: its commits between
173	- `X.Y.Z-3`: its Close-out
174	- `X.Y.Z-3.1.0`: Preparation of the `-3.1` sub-sub-cycle
175	
176	Bump the version-of-record at the start of every step (the per-commit checklist carries the step),
177	so the manifest always records the commit it will be part of and, per the preference above, every
178	commit carries a distinct version.
179

  adds its case to [Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record).

Two reservations keep the remap sound:

- **The stored version identifies but does not order.** SemVer sorts a suffixed version *before* its
  bare release (matching cycle semantics: rungs precede close-out), while PEP 440 sorts the remapped
  form *after* it, and reinterprets a lone `-N` as a post-release. Opposite directions, so no
  cross-medium logic may compare stored versions. Ordering truth lives in the ladder and git
  history. Comparing the public triple alone (e.g. a version gate) is unaffected.
- **`+` is reserved** for the PEP 440 remap: no SemVer build-metadata use in Rust repos even though
  Cargo allows it, since spending `+` there breaks the bijection with the Python spelling. A repo
  that truly needs it declares the deviation in its `custom.md`.

## Recording the version-of-record

Where the version-of-record lives, how it's stored and surfaced, and how often it changes. Pick the
case that fits your medium:

- **Manifest**, where the version-of-record is stored:
  - if Rust, `Cargo.toml` `[package].version`
  - if Python, `pyproject.toml` `[project].version` (or the committed config it's sourced from)
  - otherwise wherever the medium records it (a generic `version.toml`, a book's frontmatter, ...).
    Add the case as needed
- **Notation**, how the `-` form is stored. See [Grammar and storage](#grammar-and-storage):
  - if the format allows `-` (TOML `version.toml`, `Cargo.toml`), store it verbatim
  - if it bars `-` (PEP 440's local segment, e.g. a Python project), remap to `+`, so `0.3.0-5.3.0`
    becomes `0.3.0+5.3.0`: same version, just the stored spelling
- **Reporter**, how a built artifact surfaces the version-of-record:
  - if a CLI app, `<cli-app> -V`
  - if a TUI/GUI, add to Help/About or display on the title
- **Cadence**, how often to bump: see [Unique per
  commit](#unique-per-commit-preference-not-requirement). This project follows the per-commit
  preference.

## Dev artifact name

When other projects consume the built artifact (e.g. the installed CLI) while this repo is under
active development, the dev build installs under a separate name so a mid-cycle install never
clobbers the binary consumers are running:

- **Name**: the manifest's package name carries a `-dev` suffix (`<name>` -> `<name>-dev`). If Rust,
  `[package].name`, so the per-commit flow's `cargo install` produces `<name>-dev` and leaves plain
  `<name>` untouched.
- **Constant, not per-step**: the step already lives in the version-of-record (`<name>-dev -V`
  reports the exact rung). A per-step name would churn the manifest every commit and litter the
  install dir with stale binaries.
- **Promotion**: plain `<name>` updates only by an explicit act: a separate clone built at the
  chosen commit with the plain name (or a copy of the dev binary), never by the per-commit flow's
  install.

**Single-name variant**: a repo striving to release makes the package name the binary's name, plain
`<name>` on `main` only:

- **The opening renames**: its bump sets `<name>-dev` beside the suffixed version, and every rung
  and the closing build under the dev name, the closing over the bare version.
- **Land restores**: the rename back to `<name>` is Land's act, so the stable name is only ever
  installed from what `main` will carry.
- **A build script guards the pairing** on every cargo verb: a suffixed version under the stable
  name fails the build, so no mid-cycle install can clobber the consumers' binary.

## Unique per commit (preference, not requirement)

Our general notion is that the version-of-record should change on **every commit**, so a built or
running artifact identifies the exact commit it came from.

- This is a preference, **not** a hard requirement. A project following the cycle protocol may bump
  less often: once per cycle, only at release, and so on. Record the choice in [Recording the
  version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record) if it differs.
- It is achievable because the cycle's versions (below) are **pre-assignable**, unlike the git SHA,
  which a commit cannot contain.

## Suffix scheme

The cycle (opening -> commits -> closing, per the [Cycle protocol](../AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol))
encodes each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a
Preparation**.

This is the manifest's own spelling, read by whoever inspects `Cargo.toml` or `-V` output. It is not
a name for a step: a step is identified by its title, and an in-flight ladder rung carries neither a
number nor a version (see [Steps are named, not numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)).
The identifiers below count commits within a phase, and nothing dereferences one.

- `X.Y.Z-0`: Preparation
- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, ...: the commits between
- `X.Y.Z`: Close-out (bare version, no suffix)

**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle, with no ladder and no setup commit, skips `-0` and
starts at `-1` (its first commit). A single-step cycle is one commit, the Close-out, and carries the
bare `X.Y.Z` ([Cycle shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle
needing no Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that grows a Preparation later adds the `0`
step without renumbering siblings.

Disambiguation:

- `-10`: commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a Preparation.
- `-1.0`: Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final identifier `0`).

**Nesting.** Sub-cycles append another level, recursively:

- `X.Y.Z-3.0`: Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle
- `X.Y.Z-3.1`, `X.Y.Z-3.2`: its commits between
- `X.Y.Z-3`: its Close-out
- `X.Y.Z-3.1.0`: Preparation of the `-3.1` sub-sub-cycle

Bump the version-of-record at the start of every step (the per-commit checklist carries the step),
so the manifest always records the commit it will be part of and, per the preference above, every
commit carries a distinct version.

above). The shared template:

```

<optional prose intro>
  - <optional item>
    <optional prose intro>
      - <optional sub-item>
      ...

  title (see the protocol's [Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), bulleted, never `;`-joined inline.

title line up verbatim. The rung's subsection heading carries the same title, a third
surface on every rung (the closing rung's exists only when close-out gotchas occurred: see the

title, never one shared cycle title uniquified by a step marker. The block's title heading carries
the *cycle title*, the bare name no multi-step commit carries (see the bookends below). To keep a
cycle's commits collectable with one `git log --grep`, give the step titles a common greppable stem

them scannable. Rungs between keep their own titles on the stem.

### Commit titles and descriptions

([why](rationale.md#commit-titles-and-descriptions))

The vocabulary over the structure: [Conventional-commit
shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit) holds what a title and body are shaped like, and
this section holds what may fill them. The title is a [Conventional
Commit](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/), `<type>: <short description>` with an optional
`(scope)`, at the width in [Line widths](#line-widths). The body is the [Commit-body
form](#commit-body-form), wrapped per Line widths, with no version in title or body, no file list,
and no deliberation. `vc-x1 push` gives both repos' commits the same title and body. `ochid:` is
the body's last line, stamped by push, and a breaking change uses the hyphenated
`BREAKING-CHANGE:` trailer key.

#### Conventional commit types

The common types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `test`, `docs`, `chore`. A type beyond the common set
is a declared one ([Project-declared types](#project-declared-types)), and a title check admits
exactly the two vocabularies.

#### Conventional commit scopes

A scope names a component as its user would name it (a subcommand, a repo), never a file or
directory, and is omitted when there is none. A declared type's scope slot carries its
declaration's vocabulary instead ([Project-declared types](#project-declared-types)).

#### Project-declared types

Beyond the common types, a project may declare its own when a recurring kind of work deserves one

- `agent-files`, the set's own lifecycle: `agent-files(<scope>): vX.Y.Z`, the description being the

  version](versioning.md#agent-files-version)), which keeps the formulaic titles unique and is the

    - `proposal`, outbound work for others to adopt. The cycle bumps the agent-files version, and

  format](notes.md#todo-format)), so no rank number exists to be cited (the numbered form retired

### A single-step cycle is two stages and one commit, and the last record has a file of its own

(wink + agent, 2026-10-11) Tried by the cycle **docs: update single-step cycle add zCLOSED.md**,
whose record has the reasons, and wink liked how it read. A single-step cycle is one commit that
records its own acceptance check as passed before the commit exists, and an opening deletes the
last finished record, so none is readable while a cycle runs. An `agent-files` proposal makes the
trial the rule or drops it.

- Two stages, each validated, reviewed, and pushed: the first carries the opening's duties and
  the work, under the dev name at the `-1` suffix. The closing runs the acceptance check against
  the pushed work, sets the bare version, and moves the record.
- One work commit: the closing is folded into the pushed work commit, which keeps its change id
  and gains a second `ochid:` trailer, and the agent-repo carries a commit for each stage, both
  naming the one work commit. Done by hand in the trial, and [push --amend folds a stage into the
  pushed work commit](#push---amend-folds-a-stage-into-the-pushed-work-commit) is the tool for it.
- One way of running: a single-step cycle and a multi-step one then open and close alike, and
  [Cycle shape](AGENTS.md#cycle-shape) loses its rule about the first push and the way out it
  gives a single-step cycle that grows. Whether a multi-step closing folds too is open.
- Land restores the plain name in both, as a multi-step cycle's does today.
- The one commit lands as it is, with no merge commit, and `main` is pushed once.
- The bookmark's create and publish needs no approval. The pushes and the Land keep theirs.

  of its own, `zCLOSED.md`. Two blocks in one file were tried first and collided on reference
  numbers and on the item headings' anchors.
- The ladder is one unlinked rung with the bare title, as today, and no title carries
  " closing". What the closing taught goes under a `#### Closing` heading in the block.
- It rides with, or after, [The cycle-record moves out of TODO.md into

[package]
name = "vc-x1"
version = "0.84.22"
edition = "2024"

# Single-name convention (chores-16, 0.78.3): the package name IS
# the installed binary's name, `vc-x1` on main and a per-line dev
# name on a branch (renamed at cycle open, back at close-out, next
# to the version bump). The guard against a forgotten open-rename
# is build.rs, which refuses to build a suffixed version under the
# stable name on every cargo verb, `cargo install` included.

[lints.clippy]
# The process-spawn ban: `Command::new` is disallowed via
# clippy.toml's `disallowed-methods`, and deny (not warn) so a bare
# new spawn site fails `cargo clippy` even without `-D warnings`.
# The documented allowlist lives in clippy.toml.
disallowed_methods = "deny"

[dependencies]
chrono = { version = "0.4", default-features = false, features = ["now"] }
clap = { version = "4.6", features = ["derive", "wrap_help"] }
clap_complete = { version = "4.6", features = ["unstable-dynamic"] }
futures = "0.3"
# The gix jj-lib 0.45 resolves (no features of our own): the
# session's lock-contention downcast needs type identity with the
# errors jj-lib returns, and init's bare-repo creation reuses it.
gix = { version = "0.87", default-features = false }
# When raising jj-lib: check whether it now offers the commits a
# remote's bookmarks are on without fetching. If so, `git_command`
# in src/jj/session.rs and its two callers take it, and
# clippy.toml's register entry 6 closes (TODO.md > ## Waiting).
jj-lib = "0.45"
log = { version = "0.4", features = ["std"] }
pollster = "1.0"
serde_json = "1"

[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]
libc = "0.2"

content.content:
11	## Prose form
12	
13	([why](rationale.md#prose-form))
14	
15	Long-lived prose on this project follows one basic shape: a short intro that explains the *why* or
16	the high-level *what*, sharpened to a *problem statement* where a surface calls for one (see
17	[Problem-first shape](#problem-first-shape)), then a `-` bullet list for the details. The width
18	numbers and the wrap discipline live in [Line widths](#line-widths) below, their one home. One fact
19	per bullet or sub-bullet beats a paragraph packing several. Avoid wall-of-prose paragraphs: they
20	hide the structure that bullets make scannable. Punctuation that joins clauses without naming their
21	relationship is the same failure at sentence scale. See [Semicolons](#semicolons) and [Typeable
22	punctuation only](#typeable-punctuation-only).
23	
24	Surfaces that use this shape:
25	
26	- Module / function / struct / field doc comments in `.rs` files. See [Doc
27	  comments](code.md#doc-comments-on-every-file-function-and-method).
28	- Commit message bodies (both work-repo and agent-repo). The title is the commit-specific add-on.
29	  See [The per-rung flow](../AGENTS.md#the-per-rung-flow).
30	- The cycle-record, `TODO.md > ## In Progress`. See [The In Progress
31	  block](notes.md#the-in-progress-block).
32	- Todo entries in `TODO.md` when an entry needs more than one line of detail. Pure one-liners are
33	  still fine.
34	
35	Bullet *content* differs by surface:
36	
37	- **Commit bodies**: the [Problem-first shape](#problem-first-shape) for finished work, arranged by
38	  [Commit-body form](#commit-body-form) below. What is specific to a commit:
39	  - the problem statement defines any word the title assumes, since the title is what a reader meets
40	    first and it answers the problem
41	  - **no file list.** The diff and `git show --stat` are the mechanical record, so restating them is
42	    a second copy that can drift from the first. An import of a thousand files is one change
43	  - these are claims a reader has to follow, so they are sentences rather than fragments. A bullet
44	    wanting a paragraph belongs in the cycle-record instead
45	  - the **deliberation** stays out: alternatives weighed, evidence, dates, costs accepted. Those
46	    live in the cycle-record, the `## Todo` entry, and the session the `ochid:` trailer names, each
47	    reachable from the commit by construction. The problem itself is a *why* and belongs here
48	- **Cycle-record / todo**: bullets are conceptual (design points, structural notes, the "what landed
49	  and why" at a notch above file-list granularity). Never a copy of the commit's edit list. The diff
50	  is the mechanical record, the commit body the problem and solution, the cycle-record the design
51	  thinking, and none restates another.
52	- **Doc comments**: bullets are whatever structure fits (fields, cases, invariants).
53	
54	### Leads are labels, unmarked
55	
56	In a list item or a numbered step, a lead is a short label ending in a colon, with no markup, and
57	the sentence after it is complete without it:
58	
59	```
60	1. Backfill: fill every as-built ladder whose commits have landed, before anything else.
61	```
62	
63	- Label names, sentence instructs: a reader's eye takes bold at the head of an item as the item's
64	  name and resumes at the plain text expecting a full sentence, so a bold lead that is the
65	  sentence's own verb or subject (`**Backfill** every as-built ladder ...`) loses its imperative to
66	  the reader who skips it. Measured 2026-08-21, at the review of the rule that example is from: the
67	  reviewer read "every as-built ladder" and stopped, with nothing telling them what to do.
68	- The inverted case: a rule stated in bold is the same failure inverted. When the bold is a whole
69	  sentence and the plain text is commentary, the reader who skips bold reads the commentary as the
70	  rule. The fix is the same: a short name as the label, the rule as the plain sentence. The hard
71	  rules in AGENTS.md are the instance, and the names they gained are greppable and survive a
72	  renumbering.
73	- Definitions: the same shape, `Term: what it means.` A period after a bold term (`**Term.** ...`)
74	  reads as a heading, which is the label reading again.
75	- No markup on the label: bold is what makes the eye treat the lead as a heading and skip it, and
76	  the agent-files are read by an agent, which needs no emphasis. The colon alone marks the label
77	  (wink, 2026-08-21).
78	- The price: one word of redundancy, paid on purpose: the label is skippable, the sentence is not.
79	
80	### One spelling per term
81	
82	A defined term has one spelling, everywhere: `work-repo` and `agent-repo` are always hyphenated,
83	`agent-files`, `version-of-record`, `dual-repo`, and `as-built` likewise, and no rule varies the
84	spelling by how the term is used. Terminology in AGENTS.md defines the terms, and this section is
85	where the spelling rule lives, since a glossary is read for meaning rather than for spelling.
86	
87	### Bullet form
88	
89	A bullet is a full sentence, capitalized and ending in a period or question mark, unless the list
90	is a plain list of things (files, names, options), which takes neither. A list is all one or all
91	the other. A sentence never opens with a lower-case name (`squash-push`, `rationale.md`), it is
92	recast so the name is not the first word.
93	
94	### Line widths
95	
96	Every width number lives here and nowhere else: the other files and sections link here rather than
97	restating one, so a change is a single edit and the copies cannot drift. Consolidated 2026-08-09,
98	when the body width moved and the restatements had to be hunted.
99	
100	- **Prose**, all durable text: wrap at <=100 cols, bullet continuations indented two spaces.
101	- **Source**, doc comments and inline comments included: <=100 cols, which is rustfmt's default
102	  `max_width` (enforcement notes in [code.md](code.md#line-width)).
103	- **Commit titles**: <=50 chars.
104	- **Commit bodies**: <=75 cols, the Linux kernel patch standard. It replaced git's older 72
105	  convention here 2026-08-09, and published bodies keep the wrap they shipped with.
106	
107	The widths are wrap defaults, not absolutes (the title cap excepted). Existing text re-wraps when
108	touched, no mass sweeps. Write to the full width: wrap near the limit rather than imitating the
109	narrow wrap of older text, and a line that reads better long stays long (an URL, a literal report
110	row, indented code in a comment).
111	
112	### Problem-first shape
113	
114	`## In Progress` cycle blocks, `## Todo` entries, and commit bodies use a sharper form of the same
115	shape: a problem, then how it is answered, then the steps that get there.
116	
117	- **Problem statement** (the why): one or two sentences. Don't pad with intent, don't restate what
118	  follows it.
119	- **Solution statement** (the what/how): what is done about the problem, in broad terms, answering
120	  whatever question the problem statement raises. Surface-specific rules are in [Bullet content
121	  differs by surface](#prose-form) above.
122	- **Plan bullets** (the what/when), the steps. Formality differs by surface:
123	  - In Progress: a committed ladder, one step per commit. See [Conventional-commit
124	    shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit) for the per-step title + `(current)` /
125	    `(done)` form.
126	  - Todo entries: rough informal bullets, no numbering, formalized only when the entry is picked up
127	    into a cycle.
128	
129	**Timing decides whether the solution statement is provisional, not whether it is written.** A cycle
130	writes one at Preparation, before the work, and revises it as steps land. The close-out's commit
131	body carries the final one. A `## Todo` entry's is provisional in the same way. Only a commit body's
132	is settled, because a commit is finished by the time it has one. The earlier rule here said a plan
133	was for work not yet done and a solution for work that is, which left a cycle unable to say at its
